opening_message:
Ticket 1: Christopher Myers (employee ID E012) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E012.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Christopher Myers (E012) is a full-time Analyst requesting write access to Source Code. As a full-time employee, write is permitted (admin is only for the owning Engineer role). Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E012 (Christopher Myers) is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time as previously noted. Contractors with basic training max out at read. Requested write to Source Code exceeds max, so recommend granting read.
reason: E012 (Christopher Myers) requested write access to Source Code. The Security DB note indicates he is a contractor with basic security training (correcting the earlier note that he was full-time). Contractors with basic training are capped at read; write exceeds the maximum, so the maximum of read is granted. Granting no more than requested, the final level is read.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee: Christopher Myers (E012), requests write access to Source Code.

Two notes from memory with conflicting facts:
- Note 1: role Analyst, employment type full_time, recommendation write. Says full-time employee write is permitted.
- Note 2: role Analyst, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation read. Says contractor with basic training max out at read.

There's a conflict: Note 1 says full_time, Note 2 says contractor. The Security agent's note (note 2) corrects the earlier note, claiming security DB shows contractor with basic training.

Who is more reliable? The Security DB presumably is authoritative on employment type and security training. Note 1 was possibly based on incomplete info. The Security note says "Security DB shows E012 is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time as previously noted."

So according to the most recent/corrected info: contractor, basic security training. Contractors: read, or write if they have advanced security training. Never admin. With basic training, max = read.

Requested write exceeds max read, so grant maximum = read. Never grant more than requested (read is less than write anyway).

Decision: read.

Evidence: Security note says contractor with basic training; max is read; requested write exceeds max; grant read.
